PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL

 Prof. Sindhu R Pai
PCPS Theory Anchor - 2024
Department of Computer Science and Engineering

Source slide page 2 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Modules – Import mechanisms

Module

•  In Python, a module is a file that contains code.

•   It can include functions, classes, variables or any runnable code.

•  Basically, a module contains code to perform specific tasks.

• We can use modules to separate code in separate files based on their
   functionality.

Source slide page 3 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Modules – Import mechanisms

Advantages of Modules

•  Reusability - makes the code reusable

•  Modularity – Organizing the code into modules logically

•  Separate scopes – separate namespace is defined by the module

•  Grouping - Python modules help us to organize and group content by
   using files and folders

Source slide page 4 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Modules – Import mechanisms

Packages and Namespace

•  Modules in Python can be grouped together into packages.
•  Packages organize the code into logical groups and provide a namespace to
   the modules so that they don’t conflict with modules with the same name
   in other packages.
•  The import statement can also be used to import modules from a package,
  which allows to access the functions and classes defined in the package’s
  modules.

Source slide page 5 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Modules – Import mechanisms

Packages vs. Modules vs. Libraries

•  Modules – contain several functions, variables, classes etc.
•  Packages – contain several modules.
                 - folder that contains various modules as files.
•  Library - a collection of packages and modules used to access built-in
   functionality

Source slide page 6 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Modules – Import mechanisms

Types of Modules

1.  Built-in Modules
    •   Python's standard library comes bundled with a large number of
      modules.
    •  They are called built-in modules.

2.  User-defined Modules
    •  Any  file with .py extension and containing Python code  is a
      module.
    •    It can contain definitions of one or more functions, variables,
       constants, classes etc.

Modules – Import mechanisms

User-defined Modules

•  Any file with .py extension and containing Python code is a module.
•   It can contain definitions of one or more functions, variables, constants
   as well as classes.
•  Any object from a module can be made available to the interpreter or
   another Python script by using import statement.

Source slide page 10 (extracted text):

Creating a Module

•  Crete a file with .py extension
•  Example: Creating a module (module1.py)

   print("Welcome to Module-1")
   def f1():
         print("in f1")
   def f2():                                   module1.py
         print("in f2")
   def _f3():
         print("in f3")

Source slide page 11 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Modules – Import mechanisms

Importing a Module
• When the interpreter encounters an import statement, it imports the
  module if the module is present. Otherwise, ModuleNotFoundError is
  thrown.

•  Syntax -  import module_name
      import – the keyword used to import the module
      module_name – name of the module to be imported

•  To access the functions inside the module the dot(.) operator is used.

__doc__ variable
•  In Python, each object(class, function, variable,..) can be documented using
   Docstrings.
•  Docstrings can be accessed using the __doc__ attribute.

PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Modules – Import mechanisms

__name__ variable and Modules
•   It is a special variable in Python.
•   If the source file is executed as the main program, the interpreter sets the
  __name__ variable to the value “__main__”.
•   If this file is being imported from another module, __name__ will be set to
   the module’s name.

Source slide page 26 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Modules – Import mechanisms

Modules - Summary

• A Python module is a script file that can contain variables, functions,
  and classes.
•  Python modules help us organize our code and then referencing them
   in other classes or python scripts.

•  Modular programming  is the practice of segmenting a single,

  complicated coding task into multiple, simpler, easier-to-manage

   sub-tasks. These sub-tasks are the modules.
